links.site_note: URL as listed by Political Revolution; the site could not be opened from this environment.

oneliner.t: Registered nurse and patient advocate making her first run for office, who won the July 21, 2026 Democratic primary for the open AZ-05 seat with 66.0% and faces Republican Mark Lamb on Nov. 3.

upbringing.t: Her campaign website, per FOX 10, describes growing up in poverty. Ballotpedia, drawing on her survey, lists Dover High School, a bachelor's degree from Northwestern State University (2005) and an associate degree from Carrington College of Nursing (2013). No independent record of her birthplace, family or residence was found.

profile.education_note: Self-reported via Ballotpedia's survey; not independently verified.

career.role: Nurse, consultant and healthcare advocate; describes herself as a board-certified reproductive health and infertility nurse and board-certified patient advocate

platform.t: Supports Medicare for All and expanding Medicare to cover mental health, dental, vision and hearing (campaign site per FOX 10); calls access to care a right.
Would push for higher taxes on the ultra-wealthy and large corporations.
Wants to curb corporate and private-equity purchases of homes.
Opposes diverting public money to private schools.
Secure the border while creating a path to citizenship for Dreamers.
Automatic and same-day registration, expanded early and mail voting, national anti-gerrymandering standards.

promises.t: Use the House's revenue power to raise taxes on the ultra-wealthy and large corporations.

claims.claim: Would be the first woman to represent the district.

said.where: Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey; repeated in Political Revolution profile

record.t: Every representative of AZ-05 since 1983 (McNulty, Kolbe, Hayworth, Mitchell, Schweikert, Salmon, Biggs) has been a man.
No independent record (university or news) found.

claims.claim: Associate degree, Carrington College of Nursing (2013).

record.t: No independent record found; AP and KJZZ describe her as a nurse.

claims.claim: Board-certified reproductive health and infertility nurse.

record.t: Arizona Board of Nursing license lookup and certifying-body records were not reachable.

research_notes: Thin public record: first-time candidate with no prior office. Ballotpedia's survey is self-reported. Political Revolution's profile wrongly says she faces Andy Biggs (he is running for governor). Ballotpedia lists a Green candidate Richard Grayson for the general, but the verified ballot file shows only Lee and Lamb. Photo not retrieved.
